mkdir -p /workspace/project/apps/inktest && cd /workspace/project/apps/inktest && cat > app.py <<'EOF'
import http.server, json, os
class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(s):
        b=json.dumps({"ok":True,"msg":"halo dari INK","ts":os.environ.get("TZ","")}).encode()
        s.send_response(200); s.send_header("Content-Type","application/json")
        s.send_header("Content-Length",str(len(b))); s.end_headers(); s.wfile.write(b)
    def log_message(s,*a): pass
http.server.HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0",int(os.environ.get("PORT","8080"))),H).serve_forever()
EOF



cat > package.json <<'EOF'
{"name":"inktest","version":"1.0.0","scripts":{"start":"python3 app.py"}}
EOF


cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY app.py .
ENV PORT=8080
CMD ["python3","app.py"]
EOF



git init -q 2>/dev/null; git add -A; git -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@t commit -qm init; ls; echo "---"; export PATH="$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$PATH"; ink deploy --help 2>&1 | head -30
Dockerfile  app.py  package.json
---

  Creates a new service from a git repo or Docker image. For git repos, the repo
  must exist first — create one with 'ink repo create' (Ink-managed) or use a GitHub
  repo with the GitHub App installed. The service endpoint is returned by Ink after creation.

  To update or redeploy an existing service, use 'ink redeploy'.

  USAGE

    ink deploy <name> [--flags]

  EXAMPLES

    # Ink-managed repo
    ink repo create myrepo
    git remote add ink <remote-url-from-output>
    git push ink main
    ink deploy myapi --repo myrepo

    # GitHub repo (requires GitHub App installed)
    ink deploy myapi --host github --repo myorg/myrepo

    # Docker image (skips build)
    ink deploy mynginx --image nginx:latest --port 80

    # With options
    ink deploy myapi --repo myrepo --memory 512Mi --vcpu 0.5 --env-file .env
    ink deploy static-root --repo myrepo --buildpack static
    ink deploy static-dist --repo myrepo --buildpack static --publish-dir dist
    ink deploy spa --repo myrepo --publish-dir dist
